title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous pages are 8 May 1986 footnotes to Récoltes et Semailles (the Kashiwara/Mebkhout affair). This page opens with 'Après cette longue digression, il faudrait revenir à l'axiome des rapports dans un atelier'. So 'atelier' names an axiomatic structure Grothendieck was building in these notes, and this page proves a technical lemma for it.

Setting (as far as can be inferred): Σ is a complete lattice (arbitrary Sup and Inf) with an order-reversing involution ∁ ('complément'), and 1_Σ is its top element. The structure looks like an orthocomplemented lattice in the sense of quantum logic.

Lemma 1. Let e_I = (e_i)_{i∈I} be a family of nonzero, mutually disjoint elements with ∨_i e_i = 1. The following are equivalent:
(i) the e_i lie in a subset Σ_{e_I} ⊂ Σ that is stable under Sup, Inf and ∁, and is a Boolean algebra for the induced structure.
(ii) put e_J = Sup_{i∈J} e_i for J ⊂ I. The map P(I) → Σ, J ↦ e_J, which obviously commutes with arbitrary Sup, also commutes with ∁. By De Morgan it then commutes with arbitrary Inf.

Marginal NB: this map is injective, since J = {i ∈ I | e_i ≤ e_J}.

The next page completes the picture:
- The image of the map is the smallest Σ' ⊂ Σ with the properties in (i).
- Corollary: if ∨e_i = e ≠ 1, adjoin e_0 = ∁e. The family is 'admissible' (generates a Boolean algebra isomorphic to P(I ⊔ {0})) iff for every partition I = I' ⊔ I'' one has ∁e_{I'} = e_{I''} ∨ e_0, equivalently e_{I'} = e ∧ ∁e_{I''}.

In modern terms: when does an orthogonal partition of unity in an ortholattice generate a complete Boolean subalgebra, isomorphic to the power set of the index set? The answer is exactly when the 'partial sums' are complemented compatibly. This condition is an orthomodularity/compatibility condition on the family.

Purpose: presumably to give meaning to 'rapports' (ratios, possibly measure-like quantities) on the Boolean pieces of an 'atelier'. The page itself does not say this.
errors: Injectivity (J = {i | e_i ≤ e_J}) needs 'disjoint' to mean orthogonal (e_i ≤ ∁e_j) together with x ∧ ∁x = 0. Then for i ∉ J one gets e_J ≤ ∁e_i, so e_i ≤ e_J forces e_i = 0. If 'disjoint' only means e_i ∧ e_j = 0 in a non-distributive lattice, injectivity can fail. This hypothesis is implicit, not stated.

(i)⇒(ii) uses infinite distributivity of meets over joins in the complete Boolean subalgebra. This holds because the subalgebra is stable under arbitrary Sup of Σ, so it is fine, but it is not spelled out.
The underlying structure on Σ ('opérateur'?) is not defined on this page; whether x ∧ ∁x = 0 is an axiom cannot be checked here.

ideas.what: Criterion for an orthogonal family summing to 1 in a complete lattice with involution to generate a complete Boolean subalgebra ≅ P(I): the map J ↦ Sup_{J} e_i must commute with complement.
ideas.modern_name: Compatible (commuting) orthogonal decompositions / blocks in orthomodular lattices; complete atomic Boolean subalgebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff–von Neumann (1936); Foulis, Kalmbach (1960s–80s, orthomodular lattice theory)

ideas.what: Condition e_{I'} = e ∧ ∁e_{I''} for every partition, defining 'admissible' families.
Axiomatic notion of 'atelier' with an 'axiome des rapports'.
ideas.modern_name: unclear (possibly a lattice-based framework for measures/ratios, quantum-logic-like)

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck appears to be axiomatizing a structure ('atelier') built on a complete lattice with involution, using exactly the compatibility/orthomodularity notions of quantum logic. As far as I know he never cites or connects to that literature. The lemma itself is routine.
missed.quote: il faudrait revenir à l'axiome des rapports dans un atelier. Lemme 1 Soit Σ un ... e_I = (e_i) une famille d'éléments de Σ mutuellement disjoints, non nuls, et tels que ∨ e_i = 1_Σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only of historical interest: it documents an unknown 1986 foundational project ('ateliers') whose aims are not visible from this page alone.

deep.surprise_reason: The lemma is an elementary and correct lattice-theoretic fact, standard in orthomodular lattice theory. The only point of interest is that Grothendieck was building an axiomatic 'atelier' theory of this kind in 1986, which is a historical curiosity rather than a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Soit Σ un opérateur [?]': the word is illegible; possibly 'opérateur' or an 'ortho-' structure name. Uncertain.
'mutuellement disjoints, non nuls, et tels que ∨_i e_i = 1_Σ'. The crossed-out words are 'Soit telle que'.
'L'ens des e_i est contenu dans un sous-ensemble Σ_{e_I} de Σ stable par Sup, et Inf et ∁, et qui, pour la structure induite de ∁ involution, est une "alg. de Boole"'. Crossed out: '∨, ∧, ∁, et qui'.
In (ii), 'Pour tout J ∈ P(I)' replaces a crossed-out 'L'ensemble'.
The end of (ii) should read: '(qui commute évidemment aux Sup quelconques) commute à ∁ (donc aussi aux Inf quelconques)'. The machine transcription duplicates lines.
Marginal note (bottom left, rotated): 'NB cette application est injective (puisque J = {i∈I | e_i ≤ e_J})'. The 'ou' is probably 'car'/'puisque' or a separate word.
